audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows argued against themselves. Levels 2 and 3 were marked Jax while whys[1] and whys[2] both say Camille out-trades him and 'owns 3'; Levels 4-5 was Skill while whys[3] says her W-cone heal, Q shred and E mobility out-trade you; first item was Jax while whys[5] explicitly calls it a reset with 'not a stat lead'.
audit.why: The packet levelChart reads Skill / Camille / Camille / Camille / Skill / Skill / Jax, matching the written reasons. Jax at 51.83% over 928 games survives her 2-5 window and wins the two-item side lane.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Skill, Levels 2 through 5 Camille, Level 6 Skill, first item Skill, two items Jax.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why and breakdown.late name Jax's ult 'Grandmaster’s Might'; the level-6 row credits it generically rather than as the thing that survives The Hextech Ultimatum.
audit.why: The content layer uses Grandmaster at Arms. Her R is 140s at rank 1 against his 110s — the longest cooldown in the lane and the reason a spent Ultimatum is Jax's window.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster at Arms (110s at rank 1) versus The Hextech Ultimatum (140s at rank 1). Camille's spikes: W and Q at 2-3, R at 6, second item. Jax's: level 3 combo, then the two-item duel.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's cooldown block and do's reduce the matchup to 'E the follow-up' on Hookshot and never state what makes her burst hurt.
audit.why: Precision Protocol's recast deals true damage, so Armor does not answer it, and Adaptive Defenses shields her against your damage type after each auto on you. Hookshot (16s at rank 1) requires a wall — in open lane the knockup is unavailable. Counter Strike (17s at rank 1) dodges attacks only, so the W cone lands through it.
audit.corrected: Hookshot needs a wall: fight in open lane and her engage stun is gone. Her Q recast is true damage — Armor does not stop it. Hold Counter Strike for the hookshot landing or her second W cast, not for poke.
sources: enemyKit Q trueDamage, P shield, E terrain/hardCC, W text

audit.whatIsWrong: One flagged suspectName is a false positive; one kit flag set is unreliable.
audit.why: 'Hold Counter Strike' is the real name with a verb. Separately, the kit file flags her R as channel/interruptible and untargetable, which contradicts Riot's own description of a dash into an anchoring zone — the mirror audit treated both as tooltip-parse misfires and nothing was written from them.
sources: enemyKit R flags vs R text
